title: Canonicalize TensorView entries by unique semantic claim key
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: TensorView construction already forbids duplicate coordinate/relation claims, making SparseTensorEntry.semantic_key unique among retained entries. Canonical-order validation and the non-canonical sort fallback still used the larger _entry_order tuple, rereading masked, value and evidence_sha256s even though those trailing payload fields can only affect ordering when two entries share the same semantic claim, which is invalid.
primary_claim: TensorView construction now validates canonical order and sorts non-canonical retained entries by the existing unique SparseTensorEntry.semantic_key. The redundant _entry_order helper and payload-dependent canonicalization path were removed. Duplicate coordinate/relation claims remain fail-closed before retention.
gardener_decision: Extend the same semantic-key uniqueness invariant used by G1-TENSOR-01BW to TensorView construction instead of retaining a second full-payload ordering abstraction. Remove _entry_order rather than adding a cache, index, planner or alternate Tensor representation.
acceptance: canonical-order validation uses only the unique coordinate/relation semantic claim
the non-canonical sort fallback uses only the same semantic claim key
TensorView construction does not require scalar, mask or evidence payload reads merely to establish entry order
the Fourfold-v2 workflow executes successfully on the exact code/test revision
the designated Python 3.12/hash-seed-0 Tensor/Forest diagnostic executes successfully
the isolated wheel build/install executes successfully
repository-wide evidence remains collection-only rather than a full-suite execution claim
no OwnerApproval, promotion, Gate transition, measured memory/latency improvement or benchmark superiority claim is created

The focused _CanonicalOrderPayloadForbiddenEntry regression enables payload-read refusal after valid entry construction, presents 128 entries in reverse semantic order, and requires TensorView to canonicalize them without reading value, masked or evidence_sha256s for ordering. The former _entry_order path would fail that probe; the semantic-key path succeeds. Existing duplicate-claim tests retain the fail-closed uniqueness boundary.
